svg.title: Electricity overview
svg.desc: Current, pd & resistance: Q = It; V = IR. Current = charge per second. Pd = energy per coulomb. A complete circuit needs a source of pd. Charge is not used up. Ammeter in series; voltmeter in parallel. Series vs parallel: Series: same I, shared V, Rtotal = R₁ + R₂. Parallel: same V, branch currents add. More paths reduce total resistance below the smallest branch R. Components: Ohmic: constant-temperature straight I–V line. Lamp heats → R rises. Diode conducts one way. Thermistor R falls when hotter. LDR R falls when brighter; both can be sensors. Circuit practicals: Wire: vary length, measure V/I; fix material, thickness and temperature. Switch off between readings. I–V: vary supply, record paired values, reverse polarity; use protective resistor with diode. Power, mains & Grid: P = VI = I²R; E = Pt = QV. UK mains: 230 V, 50 Hz ac. Live brown; neutral blue; earth green/yellow. Grid: higher V → lower I at same power → less I²R heating. Static & fields: Rubbing transfers electrons: gain → negative; loss → positive. Like repel; unlike attract. Field acts on charges without contact. Strong fields can ionise air → spark.
